title: mTLS evidence orchestration & traffic filtering notes
content:
Purpose:
This notes doc collects design guidance, an evidence automation sketch, firewall patterns and SIEM export mappings for private deployments where customers run the Redwood control plane or runtime inside their VPCs. It focuses on: RBAC v2 mapping for network-level actors, audit log schema needed for compliance evidence, an mTLS orchestration pattern (issuance/rotation/validation), network filtering recommendations (security groups / firewall rules), and concrete SIEM ingestion/query examples to verify evidence.

Context and goals:
- Target environment: customer-managed VPCs (AWS/GCP/Azure), optional on-prem islands with a short VPN or direct connect.
- Compliance objectives: generate immutable evidence of network config and authentication events for audits (SOC2, ISO27001).
- Operational objectives: minimize blast radius during cert rotation, ensure easy correlation of identity <-> network flows in SIEM, automate evidence collection for quarterly audits.

High-level architecture (textual diagram):

Customer VPC boundary
[Internet] -- IGW/NAT --> [Public Subnet: Bastion / Load Balancer] -- LB --> [Private Subnet: Redwood runtime nodes (sidecars)]
                                      |
                                      +--> [SIEM forwarder / log-collector] --> SIEM (Splunk/Elastic/Chronicle)

Key components:
- mTLS CA (customer-owned or Redwood-managed via KMS HSM integration)
- Per-node sidecar (Envoy) performing mutual TLS termination to enforce client certs
- Gateway / LB doing TLS passthrough for control-plane endpoints
- Network ACLs / Security Groups restricting ingress/egress to allowlist of services and SIEM endpoints
- Evidence agent that snapshots SG/NACL/RouteTable configs and certificate metadata to an append-only artifact store (S3/GCS) for audit

RBAC v2: network actor model and mapping
Goal: tie network actors (service identities, operators, CI jobs) to RBAC principals and reflect decisions in logs.
- Principals: service:<service-name>@<deployment>, operator:<email>, job:<ci>-<id>
- Network roles: control-plane, runtime-node, metrics-collector, audit-agent, scaler
- Enforcement points: mTLS client cert validation (primary), network ACLs (secondary), firewall rules (final)

Example RBAC mapping table (text):
- service:runtime-api -> role:runtime-node, allowed_ports: 5005, 8080 (internal), allowed_peers: service:redis, service:kv
- service:edge-proxy -> role:control-plane, allowed_ports: 8443, allowed_from: 0.0.0.0/0 (ingress from LB)
- service:audit-agent -> role:audit -> egress_allowed_to: siem-collector:5044

Audit log schema (network & auth-focused fields)
We require a unified schema so evidence automation can assemble proofs. Minimal required fields for each event (JSON lines):
- timestamp: RFC3339
- event_type: "tls.handshake" | "conn.established" | "firewall.change" | "route.change" | "cert.rotate"
- service_principal: (string) e.g. service:runtime-api@us-east-1
- src_ip: (string)
- src_port: (int)
- dst_ip: (string)
- dst_port: (int)
- tls_client_fingerprint: (sha256 hex of client cert public key)
- tls_server_fingerprint: (sha256 hex of server cert public key)
- tls_version: "TLS1.3" | "TLS1.2"
- tls_cipher: (string)
- outcome: "success" | "failure"
- failure_reason: optional string
- actor: (string) the RBAC principal that initiated the action, if available
- evidence_bucket_path: (string) pointer to snapshot artifact for config state at time of event
- correlation_id: (string) request or trace id if present

Notes: keep fields flat and searchable in SIEM. Record cert fingerprints not full certs to reduce PII/secret leakage; link to artifact store for full certs if needed for auditors under access controls.

mTLS issuance and rotation pattern (recommended):
1) Root CA stored in customer-managed KMS/HSM. Short-lived intermediate CA minted by platform orchestration (validity 2 months).
2) Automation service (cert-orch) mints workload certs with 7-14 day TTL and writes metadata to evidence bucket and to the audit log stream (event_type: cert.issue).
3) Sidecars perform strict validation against CA chain and check cert validity and OCSP where applicable.
4) Rotation flow: cert-orch pre-issues replacement certs 48 hours before expiry, pushes to nodes via secure channel (S3 signed URL + ephemeral token), sidecars hot-reload certs and emit cert.rotate events.
5) Post-rotation: evidence-agent captures post-rotation fingerprint snapshot and appends to append-only manifest (signed by orchestration key).

Key operational controls:
- All issuance/rotation actions must be recorded with correlation_id and operator identity.
- Only cert-orch service principal can write to the evidence manifest path. KMS policy + bucket policy enforced.
- Use short cert TTLs to limit window for compromised keys.

Network filtering / firewall patterns (practical guardrails)
Principles: least privilege, defense in depth, deny-by-default egress for runtime nodes except allowed destinations, centralize SIEM egress via a small fleet of log forwarders.
Suggested rule sets (cloud-agnostic):
- Control-plane nodes: inbound only from LB IPs / ALBs and from internal CIDR subnets used by infra; outbound to internal storage and monitoring endpoints only.
- Runtime nodes: deny all ingress from internet; allow ingress only from edge-proxy and control-plane IP ranges on application ports; allow egress to SIEM collectors on 5044/9200 and to package registries on 443.
- Bastion hosts: allow SSH only from company-managed jump IPs (or zero trust connector).

Example AWS security group style (pseudocode):
- sg-runtime-ingress: allow tcp 5005 from sg-edge-proxy; deny from 0.0.0.0/0
- sg-siem-egress: allow tcp 5044 to siem-collector-cidr; restrict destination port and destination IP range
- nacl-subnet: deny ephemeral high ports outbound unless explicitly whitelisted for outbound update jobs

Evidence automation sketch (artifact flow):
1) evidence-agent runs on schedule or triggered (pre-change / post-change hooks).
2) Collectors: SG/NACL/RouteTable snapshot, sidecar cert fingerprints, node metadata (instance id, AMI hash), LB config, DNS records for endpoints.
3) Snapshot is stored to evidence-bucket/<deployment>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<epoch>.json (append-only); each file signed by the orchestration signing key and accompanied by audit log entries listing file path and signature.
4) Automated ruleset validates snapshots (e.g. assert no public SG on runtime subnets) and if a violation is found, opens an incident and records remediation steps in an evidence-runbook field in the manifest.
5) SIEM ingestion pipeline consumes audit log lines and evidence-manifest metadata, linking events by correlation_id.

SIEM export & queries (example mappings)
- Ingest: forward audit log JSON lines to SIEM (prefer structured JSON ingestion). Ensure field names map (e.g., tls_client_fingerprint -> client_fingerprint).
- Tag events with deployment, environment (prod/stage), region, and evidence_bucket_path.

Splunk example query to find failed TLS handshakes and link to cert snapshot: 
index=redwood_audit event_type=tls.handshake outcome=failure | table _time, service_principal, src_ip, dst_ip, failure_reason, tls_client_fingerprint, evidence_bucket_path

Elastic/Kibana KQL example: 
event_type: "tls.handshake" AND outcome: "failure" | sort @timestamp desc | fields @timestamp, service_principal, tls_client_fingerprint, evidence_bucket_path

Detection examples to add to SIEM:
- Unexpected egress: runtime nodes sending to external IPs not in allowlist -> generate high severity alert and attach evidence manifest for time window.
- Rapid cert churn: more than X cert rotates in Y minutes for a given service -> possible automation bug or attack; escalate.
- Firewall drift: snapshot validator detects public SG assigned to runtime subnets -> open incident and attach route/SecurityGroup snapshot.

Checklist: Pre-deployment hardening (quick run):
- [ ] CA root stored in customer KMS/HSM, policy reviewed
- [ ] Cert-orch has minimal IAM policies, uses ephemeral tokens for node delivery
- [ ] Sidecars configured for strict mTLS with CA chain pinning
- [ ] SG/NACL deny-by-default applied to runtime subnets
- [ ] SIEM forwarder reachable only from dedicated collector instances
- [ ] Evidence-agent scheduled, test snapshot created and signed
- [ ] Baseline SIEM queries implemented and test alerts validated

Checklist: Incident readiness (network & certs):
- [ ] Playbook for emergency CA revocation and intermediate reissue exists
- [ ] Rollback path if sidecars fail to accept new certs (fallback to old certs for 1 hour)
- [ ] Post-incident evidence ingest verified and tamper-evident signatures present

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Determine default TTL for workload certs balancing ops overhead vs security – propose 7 days for high-security customers, 14 days for general customers.
- Should we include full cert bodies in evidence manifests or only fingerprints plus signed storage paths? (Recommend storing full certs behind restricted bucket access; keep fingerprints in logs.)
- Validate compatibility matrix for Envoy sidecar versions across customer AMIs and orchestration agent versions.

Appendix: quick troubleshooting snippets
- How to correlate: use correlation_id from request logs to find cert.issue / cert.rotate events and then look up evidence_bucket_path to see pre/post snapshots.
- If SIEM shows repeated TLS failures for a service after rotation: check cert-orch logs for failed delivery, check sidecar logs for pem parse errors, and verify KMS decrypt step succeeded.

End of notes.

Reviewer pointers: please add missing cloud-provider specific commands (AWS CLI / gcloud / az) if we want a runbook, and flag any policy names we must lock down in customer templates.
